basis: North Macedonia's reported view in the screening report is that it is fully aligned with the Broadband Cost Reduction Directive, while the Commission's 2024 report says it is yet to align with that directive.
On the same Reform Agenda step on the Law on Electronic Communications in the same 2025 assessment, the beneficiary considers it fully achieved and the Commission considers it not achieved.
On the same Reform Agenda step in the same 2026 assessment, after the December 2025 amendments, the beneficiary considers it achieved and the Commission considers it not achieved.

The ICT strategy says fixed broadband coverage of 77% of households is in line with an EU average of 78%, while the Commission's 2025 report says fixed broadband was available to 79.6% of households at the end of 2023, below an EU average of 93.1%.
ITU gives 82.8% of households with fixed broadband access in 2020, while the Commission's 2021 report gives 73.58% of households with access to broadband, with no year stated in the sentence.

The Commission's 2025 assessment says there is no data for 2022 and 2023 on households with internet at home, while the State Statistical Office series published in 2024 gives values (86.6 and 88.0) in the positions for those years.
The regulator's 2025 work report dates the start of the roam like at home regime to 1 June 2021, while the Commission dates the regional roaming-free zone to 1 July 2021.
One Commission document says the Regional Roaming Agreement entered into force in July 2019, and a later one says it entered into force on 1 July 2021.
